name: Unique city-pair distance bins fewest count
description: Unique city pairs use English city names from airports_data.city JSON (json_extract city $.en), ordered lexicographically so A-B equals B-A. Distance is Haversine with Earth radius 6371 km from airports_data.coordinates '(lon,lat)' text. Average distance across all flights between the pair, then bin with ROUND(avg_dist/1000)*1000 into 0,1000,2000,3000,4000,5000,6000+ (cap at 6000+). Return how many pairs are in the distance bin that has the fewest unique city pairs.
sql: WITH airports AS (SELECT airport_code, json_extract(city, '$.en') AS city_en, CAST(trim(substr(coordinates, 2, instr(coordinates, ',') - 2)) AS REAL) AS lon, CAST(trim(substr(coordinates, instr(coordinates, ',') + 1, length(coordinates) - instr(coordinates, ',') - 1)) AS REAL) AS lat FROM airports_data), routes AS (SELECT CASE WHEN a.city_en < b.city_en THEN a.city_en ELSE b.city_en END AS city1, CASE WHEN a.city_en < b.city_en THEN b.city_en ELSE a.city_en END AS city2, 2.0 * 6371.0 * ASIN(MIN(1.0, SQRT(POWER(SIN(((b.lat - a.lat) * pi() / 180.0) / 2.0), 2) + COS(a.lat * pi() / 180.0) * COS(b.lat * pi() / 180.0) * POWER(SIN(((b.lon - a.lon) * pi() / 180.0) / 2.0), 2)))) AS dist FROM flights f JOIN airports a ON a.airport_code = f.departure_airport JOIN airports b ON b.airport_code = f.arrival_airport WHERE a.city_en IS NOT NULL AND b.city_en IS NOT NULL AND a.city_en <> b.city_en), pair_avg AS (SELECT city1, city2, AVG(dist) AS avg_dist FROM routes GROUP BY city1, city2), binned AS (SELECT CASE WHEN ROUND(avg_dist / 1000.0) * 1000 >= 6000 THEN '6000+' ELSE CAST(CAST(ROUND(avg_dist / 1000.0) * 1000 AS INT) AS TEXT) END AS distance_range, COUNT(*) AS pair_count FROM pair_avg GROUP BY 1) SELECT MIN(pair_count) AS fewest_unique_city_pairs FROM binned
